claims.text: FCC/BCC HEA nanoscale multilayers in the as-deposited state have minimal short-range order.
The as-deposited multilayers retain intact nanoscale layering.
The as-deposited multilayers contain a baseline dislocation network.
Post-deposition annealing just below the order-disorder transition can tune the degree of short-range order through changes in annealing temperature and duration.
The degree of short-range order governs progressive plastic deformation under sustained loading in FCC/BCC HEA nanoscale multilayers.
Short-range order modulates dislocation mobility in FCC/BCC HEA nanoscale multilayers.
Enhanced short-range order increases barriers to dislocation cross-slip.
Enhanced short-range order increases barriers to dislocation climb.
Enhanced short-range order may facilitate localized recovery.
The effects of enhanced short-range order raise the threshold for dislocation motion.
Raising the threshold for dislocation motion reduces the rate of progressive plastic deformation or creep.
Annealed multilayers with increased short-range order will exhibit lower creep rates than minimal-SRO as-deposited multilayers under otherwise identical sustained loading.
Short-range order can be quantified using diffuse electron scattering or high-resolution synchrotron X-ray diffraction.
An intermediate-temperature testing regime can preserve the induced short-range-order state while avoiding complete recrystallization and phase instability.
Conventional alloy studies support the physical plausibility that short-range order affects dislocation motion.
The quantitative relationship between short-range order and creep rate in HEA multilayers is not established.
The activation energies and thresholds associated with SRO-mediated dislocation motion in these multilayers are not established.
A lack of statistically significant association between measured SRO variation and creep rate or observed dislocation mobility would reject the proposed mechanism.
